recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-26615 in the core source; future changes to MedicationKnowledge author or jurisdiction should be handled through the later MetadataResource/CanonicalResource issue family rather than this R4 formulary-jurisdiction request.
issue_request: FHIR-26615 asked to add a coded jurisdiction to MedicationKnowledge to identify the jurisdiction responsible for a formulary. The Published/Not Persuasive with Modification disposition rejected putting formulary jurisdiction on MedicationKnowledge, said formulary jurisdiction belongs on the formulary-level Composition/List, and instead directed adding a 0..1 author for the organization that created or owns the MedicationKnowledge information.
initial_application: Git commit 603de50396973db754fec17786a66ce29799296c appears to have initially applied FHIR-26615 by adding MedicationKnowledge.author as 0..1 Reference(Organization) in the historical MedicationKnowledge spreadsheet source. No Jira-tagged initial commit added the requested jurisdiction for FHIR-26615, matching the issue resolution.
additional_context: MedicationKnowledge is active in source/fhir.ini and is now defined in source/medicationknowledge/structuredefinition-MedicationKnowledge.xml. Later applied/published issues changed the interpretation: FHIR-32801 made MedicationKnowledge a MetadataResource, FHIR-45285 changed MedicationKnowledge.author from Reference(Organization) to ContactDetail for interface compatibility, and FHIR-42901 later changed intendedJurisdiction to the canonical-resource jurisdiction element. The combined branch already represents FHIR-32801 and FHIR-45285 separately; FHIR-42901 was used only as later context for this seed.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current authoritative source defines MedicationKnowledge.author as 0..1 ContactDetail and MedicationKnowledge.jurisdiction as 0..* CodeableConcept. The author concept required by FHIR-26615 remains present, while the current jurisdiction element is justified by later CanonicalResource work rather than by the rejected FHIR-26615 formulary-level jurisdiction request.
